conviction_note: The H1 beat against the company plan is close to certain: Q1 ordinary profit already covers 67.2% of the H1 plan, against a 52.8% five-year average. So the print turns on how far the full year is raised against IFIS (OP 63.5bn, ordinary 69.8bn). If the H1 beat is added and H2 is held, the full year lands at or slightly above that bar, and Koito did exactly that last October. On the other side, the company's own wording is cautious, peer Stanley held its full year and fell 11% over two sessions, and Koito's own 24% raise last year was sold (-0.7%). Hence a mild lean, p_up 58, on abs 4.0, giving +0.64. The findings sum to +1.6 because they are sized one by one and are not fitted to that number.
bar: IFIS consensus for FY2027.03 as of 2026-10-27: revenue 970.1bn, OP 63.5bn, ordinary 69.8bn, net 44.1bn, against the company plan of 933.0bn / 60.0bn / 65.5bn / 39.5bn (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=7276). Company H1 plan: OP 25.0bn, ordinary 27.5bn (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=7276&mode=k). print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of the revised FY operating-profit guide against the 63.5bn IFIS OP, roughly 65bn.
positioning_check: JPX short register 2026-10-27: no disclosed position at or above 0.5% (short_ratio 0.0, no change); a real zero, so there is no squeeze fuel. Margin ratio (信用倍率) 18.26 (baseline; kabutan shows the same 18.26x), so leveraged retail is heavily long, the lean's largest component (-0.63) and an overhang on any disappointment. No option skew exists. Tape: seven straight down sessions from 2,766 (10/16) to 2,552.5 (10/27), -7.7%, while the Nikkei rose 1.73% on 10/27 (https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=7276). Run-up: 20d -2.29%, 5d -4.38%.

findings.finding: Q1 FY2027.03 ordinary profit of 18.475bn (+46.6% YoY, 16.7% above IFIS's 15.833bn) already covers 67.2% of the 27.5bn H1 plan against a 5-year average of 52.8%. That makes an H1 beat near-certain and a full-year raise probable. Holding the 38.0bn H2 ordinary plan and adding a plausible ~33-35bn H1 puts the full year at about 71-73bn ordinary, against IFIS at 69.8bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the H1 print on 2025-10-28 Koito raised FY ordinary profit 24% (41.0bn to 51.0bn) after an H1 that beat a forecast decline. The stock went -1.08% on the day and -0.72% from the prior close to the next close, so it sold the raise. The Q1 beat on 2026-07-29 went +6.83% on the day. The FY guide on 2026-05-13 went +6.24%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. IFIS already sits about 6.6% above the company's ordinary plan, so a raise as such is expected. The unpriced part is size: IFIS OP of 63.5bn implies only ~15.6bn a quarter for Q2-Q4, about the Q1 run-rate, so a raise that simply carries the H1 beat clears it. If the market had priced a 71bn+ raise, the stock would not have fallen 7.7% over seven sessions into the print, and consensus would have moved by more than +0.3% in four weeks.
findings.independence: The company's no-pre-revision record (TDnet shows no 業績予想の修正 since 2026-05-13) fits an H1 beat that is under the 30% disclosure trigger and is being held for the release. Same document family, so this is not independent. Last year's raise-at-H1 precedent: https://s.kabutan.jp/stocks/7276/news/k202510280011/

findings.finding: Independent volume and FX series for Q2 (Jul-Sep 2026) support the H1 beat. Toyota domestic production was +12.4% in July (328,157) and -1.7% in August (204,487), about +6.5% over the two months despite the 7/28 Kumamoto quake. The H1 USD/JPY average was 159.95, against Koito's 150.0 assumption and 146.16 a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 quarter surprise (+16.7% vs IFIS) moved the stock +6.83% on 2026-07-29. Q2 last year (Jul-Sep 2025) had OP of only 7.9bn at a 3.5% margin, so the YoY comparison is easy.
findings.why_not_priced: Toyota's monthly production data and the yen are public, so this is mostly priced. What is less visible is the size of the translation effect on Koito's Americas segment (38% of Q1 sales, 91.1bn) at roughly 160 against a plan of 150. It is a macro-to-company transmission, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The FX figure comes from Stanley Electric's H1 supplementary deck (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261026/140120261026555731.pdf), a different issuer. Toyota July production: https://monoist.itmedia.co.jp/mn/articles/2609/17/news018.html

findings.finding: Peer Stanley Electric released H1 on 10/26 at 15:00. It beat its own H1 OP plan by 8.3% but held the full year, and fell -7.18% and -4.08%. Its weakness was China (organic sales -26.8%, OP -65%) and a Japan segment loss tied to Honda and the quake, while the Americas grew +26.5% organically with OP +83%. Koito fell -1.17% and -1.24% on the same two days, although its mix is the inverse: China 4% of Q1 sales and loss-making at the margin, Japan Toyota-centric, Americas 38%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no recorded case of a Stanley read-through reversing on a Koito print. Koito's own last three prints moved +5.1% to +6.2% from the prior close to the next close.
findings.why_not_priced: Koito's -2.4% on the Stanley days suggests the market applied a sector read-through. If it had netted out the mix, Koito would have held flat while Stanley fell 11%. The regional split is on page 7 of Stanley's deck, not in the wire headline ('最終益15%減').
findings.independence: Koito's Q1 segment table (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501597.pdf): China sales 10.6bn with an OP loss of 0.14bn; Americas 91.1bn with OP of 3.98bn. Prices: https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=6923 and https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=7276

findings.finding: Capital returns: a 50bn buyback (up to 25m shares, 9.5%) runs to 2027-05-31, of which only 16.99bn (6.31m shares) was used by end-September. That leaves ~33bn, about 4% of the 785bn market cap. The FY dividend plan of 58 yen on 154.2 yen EPS is a 38% payout, below a reported 40%+ payout guideline, so a dividend raise alongside a net-profit raise is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend was not raised at the H1 print of 2025-10-28 (FY2026 ended at 56 yen, the same as FY2025). The buyback was announced on 2026-05-29, not at an earnings print.
findings.why_not_priced: The buyback is public and its remaining capacity is knowable, so that part is priced. A dividend raise is unannounced; the 40% payout guideline is a third-party snippet (finboard) from a mid-term plan whose period may have ended, so it is not load-bearing and is sized small.
findings.independence: Dividend plan 58 yen (28 interim / 30 year-end) in the Q1 短信: https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501597.pdf. The 40% guideline is snippet_only: https://finboard.jp/companies/JP:7276/dividends

findings.finding: The company's own Q1 outlook says the environment is 'increasingly uncertain': a prolonged Middle East situation cutting production, surging raw-material and energy costs (naphtha supply anxiety, which feeds lamp resins), and a US/China slowdown. It held the FY plan at Q1. Stanley's choice to hold its full year after an H1 beat shows a raise is not guaranteed in this sector this season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stanley holding its full year after an H1 beat went -11% over two sessions (10/26-27). Koito has not held after an H1 beat in the cases found: it raised at H1 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: The cautious wording is three months old, and the market (IFIS +6.6% above plan, Mizuho's upgrade to 3,400 on 9/29) has looked through it. If the market had weighed the risk of a hold, consensus would sit at the plan. A crowded margin long (18.26x) means a hold would find sellers.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is -0.52, mostly the margin overhang. My lean is mildly positive and cuts against it, on an H1 beat that is near-certain and a raise precedent. The strongest positive the release could carry (an FY raise above IFIS plus a dividend raise) was looked for and is plausible. The strongest negative is an FY hold like Stanley's into a crowded margin long, and it keeps p_up at 58 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative that rests on a public series goes toward 50) does not touch the one negative here, which rests on the forecast decision, not on a visible miss. But its logic also applies to a public series in the positive direction, so finding 2 (public production and FX series) was trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3 and finding 5 from -0.5 to -0.4 (the caution is three months old and public). The two trims offset, so impact_sum stays at 1.6 before and after; p_up and abs_move are unchanged.
Rule 2 (check the sign): the positives were searched first, and the one negative is offset in the set, so nothing moved on it.
Open question 4 (five-day run-in) was not applied: this name has a five-day run-out, and it is one case.
